subject: Throughput & Concurrency guardrails — mutual action plan and MOP agreement
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Eliza Park <eliza@olivemetrics.com>, Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@olivemetrics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: throughput / concurrency constraints & proposed MAP

Hi Eliza / Samir —

Thanks again for the call earlier — good discussion. This note captures the notable performance constraints you raised and the pragmatic next steps we agreed to validate during a pilot. The goal is to convert the demo learnings into an executable MOP (method of procedure) so everyone has clear acceptance criteria.

Recap of requirements you mentioned on the call:
- Target p95 latency: sub-200ms for generation up to ~512 tokens (we discussed tighter target for 256 tokens).
- First-token streaming latency: <120ms desired (ideally <100ms if we can).
- Sustained throughput: ~120 req/s baseline; burst to 300 req/s during peak batch windows.
- Concurrency: typical concurrent streams ~50; peak spikes to ~300 (short bursts).
- Error budget: <1% failed responses; <0.5% truncation/regression in coherence.

Immediate asks from our side:
1) Please attach a representative workload sample (requests per minute distribution + average tokens per request) — you mentioned you can share an anonymized sample.
2) Confirm whether any requests require guaranteed ordering across streams (i.e., strict session affinity).
3) Procurement constraints & timeline (you indicated Q3 procurement preferred; any required approvals?).

Proposed quick pilot plan (high-level) — we can adapt after we get the workload sample:
- 72-hour soak test against a dedicated 4-GPU pool (A100-class) with quantization & KV caching tuned for your payload.
- Measure: p50/p95/p99 latencies, first-token streaming latency, sustained throughput, and error rate.
- Acceptance: p95 <= 180–200ms on 512-token synthetic and <=150ms on 256 tokens; first-token streaming <=120ms; sustained 120 req/s for 72 hours; peak handling to 300 req/s for short bursts.
- Owner: Redwood ENG (Vivek) to provision; Redwood CS (Ben) to run scenario; Customer (Eliza/Samir) to provide workload & acceptance reporter.

I've attached the recording and a short SLO intake template to capture your formal targets. If that all looks good I can send a MAP with owner-level tasks and calendar invites for a kick-off.

Thanks — Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: olivemetrics-demo-recording.mp4 (link stub), SLO_request_form.xlsx
From: Eliza Park <eliza@olivemetrics.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@olivemetrics.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: throughput / concurrency constraints & proposed MAP

Thanks Mateo — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- On latency: our internal SLA for user-facing generation is p95 <150ms on 256 tokens. For some batch/analytics endpoints we can accept higher p95 for 512+. Can you confirm whether the 150ms target is realistic without moving to dedicated/isolated hardware?
- First-token streaming: 100ms is our goal; 120ms is acceptable for pilot if clearly improved in follow-up.
- Concurrency: typical is ~50 concurrent live sessions. Peak is 200–350 but usually only lasts a few minutes during daily syncs.
- Throughput: baseline 120–150 req/s, with spikes up to 300. We expect sustained baseline for business hours.

Procurement: we have a standard procurement window that would prefer a pilot in May, procurement/PO by July. We will need an SOW + pilot pricing to move forward.

I've attached a filled SLO_request_form.xlsx (high level) and a short anonymized sample trace file (not attached here, will share via Drive link).

If Redwood can demonstrate p95 <=150ms on 256 tokens with streaming first-token <=100ms during the pilot, that will check our primary acceptance box and speed procurement.

On the dedicated vs hosted question: we are open to running the pilot on Redwood's hosted infra if you can isolate a dedicated pool for the test.

Best,
Eliza
Director, Platform Engineering
Olive Metrics
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Eliza Park <eliza@olivemetrics.com>, Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@olivemetrics.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: throughput / concurrency constraints & proposed MAP

Eliza —

Appreciate the specificity, that's very helpful. Quick technical response to the asks:

- Short answer: yes, we can hit p95 ~150ms for 256-token profiles with a dedicated pool and tuned quantization. On hosted multi-tenant pools hitting 150ms consistently under spikes is risky; we recommend an isolated pool for the pilot.

- Proposed pilot config (initial):
  * Hardware: 4x A100 (or equivalent) dedicated pool for 72-hour soak.
  * Model variant: quantized 4-bit with KV cache pinned; dynamic batching with a 30ms batching window (tunable).
  * Networking: keep-alive and gRPC streaming enabled; first-token prioritization enabled.
  * Expected baseline: p95 ~120–160ms (256 tokens), p95 ~170–210ms (512 tokens) depending on batching and tokenization.

- Test plan: Redwood ENG runs synthetic and replay workloads (customer trace) side-by-side. We'll log: p50/p95/p99, first-token latency, throughput, concurrency, and error rates.

- Soak/peak tests: We can reproduce spikes up to 350 req/s for 5–10 minute windows to validate fallback and autoscale.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Mateo: confirm pilot start date (we can begin staging infra in 72 hours after agreement).
2) Eliza/Samir: upload anonymized trace + acceptance spreadsheet to the Drive link Mateo will share.
3) Engineering sync: Vivek and our infra team will share a short MOP (pilot-config.yaml) and an ops-runbook for the soak test.

I'll draft a short statement of work and pilot pricing range for your procurement team to review.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Attachment references: pilot-config.yaml (proposed), initial pricing band (inline draft to follow)
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Eliza Park <eliza@olivemetrics.com>, Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@olivemetrics.com>

Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 14:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: throughput / concurrency constraints & proposed MAP

Eliza/Samir —

Thanks — pushing this forward. I've created a short MAP with owners and dates (link below) and attached the pilot-config.yaml that Ben referenced. Summary of the MAP: 

- Task A (Customer): Upload anonymized trace + complete acceptance spreadsheet — owner: Eliza — due: 2027-05-06
- Task B (Redwood ENG): Provision dedicated 4xA100 pool in staging and validate networking config — owner: Vivek — due: 2027-05-09
- Task C (Redwood CS): Execute 72-hr soak, capture metrics, and produce acceptance report — owner: Ben — due: 2027-05-13
- Task D (Redwood Sales): Deliver SOW and pilot pricing for procurement — owner: Mateo — due: 2027-05-07

Acceptance criteria (finalized):
- p95 latency <= 180ms on 512 tokens, and p95 <=150ms on 256 tokens (measured per the attached spreadsheet)
- First-token streaming latency <=100ms (measured from request arrival to first byte)
- Sustained throughput >=120 req/s during business-hour traffic for 72 hours
- Ability to absorb peaks up to 300–350 req/s with <1.5x latency degradation and <1% error rate

Links: MAP & artifacts: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/olivemetrics/pilot-plan
HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/company/olivemetrics/records/8472

I'll send calendar blocks for a kick-off on 2027-05-10 if that date works for you; otherwise propose an alternative.

Thanks — looking forward to the pilot.

Mateo
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
